page: Microsoft Azure D64_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the Dv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The configuration provides 64 virtual CPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong multi-core capabilities and solid memory subsystem throughput. The instance achieves a strong rating in multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core tests, alongside high scores in Passmark CPU extended instructions and encryption tests. Large-block memory bandwidth is also strong, reaching 294.62 GB/sec for read-only operations and 135.63 GB/sec for write operations. However, single-core performance remains in the average range, as demonstrated by stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core metrics.

The lack of local storage requires reliance on external network-attached storage, which is a key architectural tradeoff. While the instance delivers strong performance in static web serving throughput and database operations, its utility for large-scale AI tasks is constrained. LLM inference benchmarks show average speeds for small and medium models, but text generation for large 70B models falls into the weak category at 2.61 tokens/sec due to the absence of GPU acceleration. Consequently, the D64_v5 is best suited for multi-threaded general-purpose workloads, software compilation, database operations, and high-throughput web serving rather than large-scale LLM generation.
